title: His Boat Sank Mid-Atlantic. He Lived 76 Days on a Rubber Raft: The Full Case
description:
Case 017, the full case file. Steven Callahan designed boats for a living, and he designed and built his own small sloop, Napoleon Solo. In 1981 he sailed her from America to England, then south, and in January 1982 he left the Canary Islands alone, bound for Antigua. About a week out, on a stormy night in early February, something hit the boat (he believes it was a whale) and within about thirty seconds she was swamped. She did not go straight down, so he went back aboard and dived into the flooded cabin for his emergency bag, then a cushion and his sleeping bag, and got away in a six-person inflatable life raft about six feet across. He named it Rubber Ducky. He had a few pints of water, a little food, flares, a radio beacon, a short spear gun and solar stills. The stills did not work as they should until he worked out how to fix them; with rain they gave him about a pint of water a day. Barnacles grew on the raft's bottom, triggerfish came to eat them, and then a school of dorado followed the raft across the ocean. He speared them to eat, and the big fish kept breaking his gun. Sharks, a hammerhead among them, slammed into the raft from below. Ships passed: he fired flares, his beacon was on, one ship passed within a mile, and none saw him. About six weeks in, a speared dorado drove the spear point into the raft's bottom tube and tore a hole about four inches long. For days every patch blew off when he pumped the tube up, until he pushed a fork from his mess kit through the rubber around the hole and folded it shut. He kept a log, and with three pencils lashed into a sextant he measured the stars and worked out how far he had drifted. He lost about a third of his weight and was covered in salt-water sores. On the night of his 75th day he saw the glow of land. The next day three fishermen off Marie-Galante, near Guadeloupe, drawn by the birds circling over the fish under his raft, found him. He had drifted about 1,800 nautical miles in 76 days, and by that evening he was walking again. His book, Adrift: Seventy-six Days Lost at Sea (1986), became a New York Times bestseller, and years later he was a consultant on living aboard a life raft for the film Life of Pi.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. Every person, boat, place and prop is a generic low-poly reconstruction; no likeness is attempted, and nothing from any film is shown. Staging details such as the boat shed, the cabin, the tins, the flare's path, the study, the film studio and everything Rook does (including his feather and the fork he pockets) are reconstruction, not record. The sources differ on some details: the sinking is dated 4 or 5 February 1982, seven or nine ships are reported, the hole is dated 15 or 19 March, and his weight loss is given as 40 or 44 pounds; the film uses only what they agree on. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

experiments.spine: v2 kept from the Short: cold open on the night the sloop is swamped, Rook's doubt on the swamped cabin top in the scene, then the story moves on from that moment; the background is one segment (12.8 s, 8% of the runtime) carried by labels and a drawn route.
experiments.long_learnings: plan/learnings.json asks the long-form videos for a shorter setup and a stronger mid-video reversal: the setup is a single segment, and the reversal (the spear tearing the raft) lands at 55% after the stakes have been raised by the sharks and the ships that do not stop.
experiments.rook_action: Detective actions: he lights the flooded cabin with a torch (11), counts the kit with a pencil (18), holds the still's cup to the light (21), sights along the pencil sextant and taps his beak (44), points from the birds to the fish (53). Mannerisms: brim drop (16, 32), feather shed (29), beak tap (5, 44), hat off at the jetty, eyes on the shiny fork (41), pockets the fork at the sign-off.

sound_plan.first_frame: An 'impact' at 0.02 s with the bang, then splashing; the hook text 76 DAYS / IN A RAFT for 1.8 s.
sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: calm for the shed, the sailing and the kit, tense for the dive, the stills and the hole, wonder under the raft, sad for the ships and the weight he lost, triumph for the fork and the rescue. No drums under the sad segments.
sound_plan.effects: One to four cues a shot, each tied to something visible (the planing, the splash as he climbs aboard, the bubbles, the ticks of Rook's pencil, the hammerhead's hit, the flare, the pump strokes).
sound_plan.hush: One: shot 49 (the island's lights), before the rescue.

source_notes: Eight pages were read for this run on 19 Nov 2026 through a fetch tool: both Wikipedia articles (Steven Callahan; Adrift: Seventy-six Days Lost at Sea), the Christian Science Monitor's 30 Sep 1982 interview (CSM82) and 31 Jan 1986 review (CSM86), the Yankee excerpt of his book (originally Jan 1986), the Sports Illustrated review of 7 Apr 1986 (SI86), Cruising World's Jan 2025 article on the documentary (CW) and 48 North's Dec 2020 interview (48N). NPR's 2013 Life of Pi piece refused the fetch and is not listed. Every narrated fact added for the full case is on at least two of them: he designs boats (naval architect: Wikipedia, SI86, CSM86; designing sailboats for his own company: CSM82); designed and built Napoleon Solo himself (Wikipedia x2, CSM86, CW); sailed from America to England, then south (Newport to Bermuda to England: Wikipedia x2, CSM82; Massachusetts to England: CSM86; Penzance in the Mini Transat, then La Coruna, then the Canaries: Wikipedia x2, CSM82); left the Canaries alone for Antigua in January 1982 (29 Jan: Wikipedia x2, Yankee; 28 Jan evening: CSM82; Antigua: Wikipedia x2, CSM82, CSM86, Yankee); a bang and swamped within about thirty seconds (Yankee 'BANG', 'less than 30 seconds'; CSM82 'in 30 seconds... still floating but swamped'); did not sink outright (watertight compartments: Wikipedia x2; still floating: CSM82); went back aboard and dived into the cabin for the emergency bag, a cushion and the sleeping bag (Wikipedia x2, CSM82, Yankee); six-person raft about six feet across (Wikipedia x2; SI86 and Yankee give 5 ft 6 in inside); lost his boat (48N, CSM82: the tether broke before daybreak); named Rubber Ducky (SI86, Yankee; CSM86 'Rubber Ducky III'); a few pints of water and a little food (CSM86 eight pints and three pounds; Yankee six pints left, a pound for four days; CSM82 'almost no food'); flares (Wikipedia x2, SI86, Yankee); radio beacon (Wikipedia x2, SI86, CSM82); short spear gun (Wikipedia x2, 48N); solar stills (three: Wikipedia x2, CSM82); the stills did not work as they should and he worked out how to fix them (48N, Yankee 'I have fixed the solar still', SI86 one did not work; the Adrift article says he cut one up to learn how they worked); about a pint a day with rain (Wikipedia x2 'just over a pint'); barnacles on the bottom (SI86, CSM82); triggerfish first, then dorado (SI86, CSM86); a school of dorado (CSM82, Wikipedia x2); the big fish kept breaking his gun (48N, Yankee); sharks and a hammerhead hitting the bottom (hammerhead: Yankee, CSM82; sharks bashing the bottom: SI86, CSM82); flares fired (Yankee, SI86), beacon on (CSM82, SI86), one ship within a mile (SI86; CSM82 two within a mile), none saw him (all); the hole about six weeks in (CSM82 day 43, 15 March; Yankee 19 March), a speared dorado drove the spear point into the bottom tube (CSM82, Yankee, SI86), four inches (CSM82, Yankee); patches blew off when he pumped (CSM82; Yankee pumping every two hours), for days (CSM82 a week; Yankee patched on 28 March); the fork from the mess kit pushed through and folded shut (CSM82, SI86); the patch held (Yankee, SI86); three pencils lashed into a sextant, the stars, his position (CSM82, SI86); his log (CW raft journal; SI86 pencils and paper pads); a third of his weight (Wikipedia x2, Yankee; 44 lb: SI86, Yankee; 40 lb: CSM82); salt-water sores (Wikipedia x2, SI86, Yankee); lights on the night of day 75 (Wikipedia x2, CSM82, Yankee 'the nighttime halo of land'); three fishermen (CSM82, CSM86, Yankee); birds over the raft drew them; they came for fish and found him (Wikipedia x2, SI86, 48N, CSM82); off Marie-Galante (Wikipedia x2, SI86, CSM82, CSM86, Yankee); 76 days (all); about 1,800 nautical miles (Wikipedia x2, CSM86; SI86 and CSM82 '1,800-mile'); walking again that evening (CSM82 'by that evening... walking unaided'; the Adrift article: in hospital for an afternoon, left that evening; the Callahan article says six weeks recovering, so the film says only that he walked that evening); Adrift, 1986 (Wikipedia x2, SI86, CSM86); a bestseller (Wikipedia, CW, 48N); consultant on living aboard a life raft for Life of Pi (Wikipedia, CW). Not used: the raft's sails, his quotes (no line is put in his mouth), the fishermen's names and boat, the 2024 documentary, his later patents, the hospital stay, the sinking's exact date and the ship count.
